summary: Where a person writes to an agent: a growing text field, a send control that becomes the stop control while a run is going, and slots for attachments and tools.
useWhen: a chat or assistant surface where the user's message starts a run
a command bar that sends free text to an agent

useInstead.when: the text is a form value submitted with other fields
useInstead.why: Enter-to-send inside a form fights the form's own submit, and a single field of a larger form is not a composer

useInstead.when: the input is a single-line search
useInstead.why: a search box does not grow, does not stop runs, and Enter means search rather than send

useInstead.when: the run needs a stop control and was not started from this composer
useInstead.why: the composer's stop belongs to the run it sent; a run started elsewhere keeps its stop beside its own activity

enter.use: the default — chat. Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line

mod-enter.use: long messages, where a stray Enter is expensive. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends and Enter is a new line

actions.note: attach, a model picker, a tool toggle — at the start of the toolbar. Icon-only buttons need their own aria-label

attachments.note: what is attached, above the text. Each removable item needs a remove control named for the file

requires: `label` — the accessible name of the field. A placeholder is not one: it disappears on the first keystroke
guarantees: the send key is described through aria-describedby, so a screen-reader user knows Enter sends before pressing it
Enter pressed while an IME is composing never sends — Japanese, Chinese and Korean input confirm candidates with Enter
while `isRunning` with `onStop`, the send control is replaced in place by AgentStop, with its guarantees: it keeps its place while stopping and announces once
focus stays in the field after sending, so the next message can be typed straight away
notes: the field stays editable while a run is going; only submitting is refused
uncontrolled, the field clears on send and a rejected onSubmit promise restores the text — unless the user has already started typing something new

antiPatterns.dont: <Textarea> beside a <Button> with an onKeyDown that checks for Enter
antiPatterns.why: the hand-built version sends mid-character for IME users and loses the prompt when sending fails

antiPatterns.dont: a separate AgentStop elsewhere on screen as well as `isRunning` with `onStop`
antiPatterns.why: two stop controls for one run raises the question of whether they do different things
the send control disables and nothing replaces it — the user can see the agent working and has no way to stop it

antiPatterns.dont: controlled `value` cleared in onSubmit before the request settles
antiPatterns.why: controlled, restoring the text on failure is the caller's job; clearing early and not restoring loses the message
